J. COMMUNITY SERVICES AND FACILITIES
Municipal Water Supply
Santa Clara Valley Water District is involved in much of the aquisition and distribution of water in Santa Clara County. The District water sources include natural ground water, surface stores water, and imported water. Throughout San Jose water is delivered to users by private water companies such as Great Oaks Water Company, San Jose Water Works and San Jose Municipal Water System. The private water companies and municipal water system obtain water by pumping ground water from wells, purchasing imported water and treating stores surface water.
Sewerage
The City is entirely served by the San Jose-Santa Clara Water Pollution Control Plant, located north of the central business disctict at the intersection of Zanker and Esteros Roads. The plant provides primary and secondary treatment of approximately 85 million gallons of effluent per day (mgd) which is outfalledinto the South Bay via the Artesian Slough to Coyote Creek. Treatment facilities are presently capable of processing 160 mgd.
Improvements are planned which will include sizing plan capabilities for 1985 loads and construction of advanced treatment (partial tertiary) facilities. A regional interceptor conveyance outfall pipe will be constructed, sized for year 2000 loads and extended north of the Dumbarton Bridge. This project will satisfy water quality objectives and eliminate outfall in the South Bay, where dilution is inadequate. Plant improvements are largely financed with Federal subsidies. An EPA restriction has been placed on the amount of funds available for plant improvements because the service area is within a critical air basin. Because of the air pollution problems, improvements are sized for 143 mgd. which reduces the net effective capacity of the plant.
San Jose's sanitary sewer system consists of six miles of interceptor lines, sixty to nenety inches in diameter, and 1,230 miles of main lines with diameters varying from ten to sixty inches.
Solid Waste Disposal Facilities and Service
Collection service in San Jose is provided by several private disposal companies under contract with the City. The waste is primarily hauled by truck to the Newby Island disposal site near Milpitas, a general purpose dump privately owned and operated. This is a cut-and-cover disposal site and is monitored for air and water pollution. The site comprises 344 acres and accepts garbage, rubbish, food processing and demolition materials from all of San Jose and Milpitas. About 1,100 tons a day of waste are accepted at the site which is expected to operate until 1985.
